newsitem.title: USA: Great Northern Iron sees lower '97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Great Northern Iron sees lower '97 earnings.

text.p: Great Northern Iron Ore Properties said Monday it expects production and earnings for 1997 to be moderately lower than 1996.

"Production and earnings for 1997 are projected to be moderately lower than those of 1996," the company said in a statement. "Barring the unforeseen, we expect 1997 to be another good year for the Trust."

Chief financial officer Thomas Janochoski said in an interview that it is too early to say how much lower, but the company expects production of taconite to be off compared with last year. He said 1996 earnings were $5.99 a share.
"We have these fluctuations up and down," Janochoski said. "Right now it's looks like it's going to be moderately lower than last year."
Great Northern Iron Ore derives its income from royalties from companies which lease and operate the ore properties owned by the Trust on the Mesabi Iron Range in Minnesota.
